ravi: noticing a hot-write cluster on scratch-us-east1-c, attach pending spiking (~90s). pulled metrics at 2026-03-23T11:03Z.
ravi: metrics: iops_p95=390k, small_write_pct=0.81, janitor_backlog=410

infra-bot: [ALERT] local-nvme write surge detected in scratch-us-east1-c. runbook: https://runbooks/redwood/scratch-iops-surge

kelly: any recent scrub or janitor changes?

ravi: scrub cadence adjusted last night (scrub-v4) and a tenant compaction batch started ~11:00Z. overlap likely.

nina: can we favor read/write coalescing by temporarily disabling janitor per-cohort? we have cohort-level knobs.

paul: cost note: diverting to dedicated would need 3 nodes warmed, est cost ~1k/hr. throttling janitor should be cheaper.

kelly: plan: 1) set cohort janitor_rate=25r/s 2) pause spot autoscale for 10m 3) increase attach worker parallelism from 2->5. if queue not below 200 in 5m, consider routing fallback.

infrastructure: executing step 1 (janitor_rate=25)

infra-bot: action recorded: janitor rate set to 25 r/s by kelly at 2026-03-23T11:07:10Z. spot-autoscale paused for 10m by ravi.

ravi: iostat after change (excerpt):
Device r/s w/s rsec/s wsec/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1: 46.00 7300.00 360.00 280000.00 720 56000 16.0 0.88 0.09 0.92 74.6

ravi: backlog dropped 410->60 in ~3m. attach median latency down 88s->14s. GPUs resuming.

nina: thumbs. Is there any risk of tombstone accumulation?

kelly: low risk; janitor slowdown increases temp retention window but doesn't change correctness. we'll run targeted cleanups later.

paul: logging cost impact and timeline for postmortem. kelly please put automated alert for janitor_backlog>300 for 2m.

kelly: created INFRA-8799 to add routing fallback + scrub scheduler enforcement.

infra-bot: incident resolved by ravi at 2026-03-23T11:06:08Z. summary: cohort janitor throttled, autoscale paused, attach workers increased.

ravi: closing thread, will follow up with postmortem draft.
